It writes each position **exactly once**.

The cursor loops guarantee this by maintaining two pointers (one for each input list) that only move forward. At each step, the algorithm compares the elements at the current positions of both lists, selects the smaller one (or the one from the first list in case of a tie), and appends it to the output list. Because the cursors never move backward and each element is consumed exactly once, every position in the output list is filled exactly once.
